email.subject: Please check your new insurance card

body.v: Your new insurance card for next year is attached. Please open it and check that your details are correct.
Cards that are not confirmed are blocked on 1 January.

hotspots.explain: The owner is the last name before the first slash: card-service.example. helveticare.example is only decoration on its left.
"Blocked on 1 January" is a threat with a date, meant to make you open the file fast.
"insurance-card.jpg.html" ends in .html. It is a web page pretending to be a picture, and it would show a fake sign-in.
Your first name is easy to find. It proves nothing.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Someone using HelvetiCare's name. The real owner of the address is card-service.example.
choices: Someone whose real domain is card-service.example

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: Fear and hurry: your card will be blocked on 1 January unless you act.
choices: Fear of a blocked card, with a date

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Open the attachment. The file is a web page that would collect your login.
choices: Reply with your date of birth

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Do not open it. Check your card in the HelvetiCare app, or call the number on your current card.
choices: Open the file to see what it is
Reply to ask for a different format
Call the number on your current card or use the HelvetiCare app

actions.label: Call the number on your current card and ask about the new one
actions.consequence: They say nothing is pending. The email was fake.

actions.label: Open the attachment to check your details
actions.consequence: A fake sign-in page opens. If you type, your login goes to the scammer.

actions.label: Reply and ask for the card in a different format
actions.consequence: The scammer sends another file. Your reply also shows your address is live.

actions.label: Report it as phishing and delete it

attacker_reveal: A picture file that ends in .html... Most people read the first extension and stop. The second one tells the browser what to do. A date on a threat helps, too.
